newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola slips on CBOT, frost fears hit grains.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola slips on CBOT, frost fears hit grains.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on lower CBOT soycomplex values and pre-weekend hedges while grains values finished lower on fears of a frost in Alberta this weekend, traders said.

"There was commercial pre-weekend hedging at the close, we hit sell stops at the lows and Chicago weighed on us," a trader said. Nov-Jan spread at $5, Nov-May $6, Mar-May $1, Sep Nov $4. Volume was 5,605 lots with 1,025 hedges.
Japan bought 2,000 tonnes of canola, sources said.

November canola fell $3 to end at $436.60. The Canadian Wheat Board forecast canola output at 4.85 million tonnes and flax at 810,000 tonnes versus StatsCan's 5.29 million tonnes and 850,000 for each, respectively.
October flax rose $2.70 to $398.50, November was steady at $372 on commercial buying, rumoured exports. Volume was 235.

October feed wheat lost $3.30 to $205.90, December down $2.70 to $190 on profit taking on fears of more feed output if there is a frost in Alberta this weekend. Oct-Mar spread at $22 on concerns of insufficient railcar allocations. Oct-May $1, Dec-May $6. Volume was 2,265 lots. Commercials bought 100 December oats fell US$3.50 at US$129.50. UGG sold 50 Oct peas down US$1.10 to US$209.90 on rumoured exports, traders said.
November western barley lost $1.10 to $149.10, February down $0.70 to $153.50 on hedge pressure. Nov-Feb at $3.50.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
